article: 秘密計算（MPC）とヤオの億万長者問題
findings: Reframed MPC privacy as a protocol-specific guarantee under an explicit adversary model, security definition, allowed inputs/outputs, and cryptographic assumptions; explained output inference, collusion, implementation, availability, and fairness limits.
Corrected BGW passive and malicious corruption thresholds in all locales and stated that Beaver triples alone do not determine a corruption threshold or provide active security.

Repaired the Bellare–Micali OT sketch: a party-known exponent cannot generate the challenge, message privacy depends on group/hash assumptions, and the formula is an educational sketch rather than an implementation specification. Distinguished Rabin OT (1981) from Even–Goldreich–Lempel 1-out-of-2 OT (1985).
Qualified garbled-circuit processing and Free-XOR cost claims, SPDZ dishonest-majority claims, and Beaver preprocessing claims; removed universal speed and certainty assertions.

Corrected the Danish auction superlative and removed unsupported claims that servers could never collude; scoped healthcare data-sharing language to applicable law, contracts, ethics, and institutional policy.
Aligned the complete Python example across all 13 editions. Each version parses and executes with matching outputs: total 2,550, mean 850.00, and population variance 3,266.67.
Added common primary-source references for Yao (1982), BGW, SPDZ, and OT; all 13 editions now share the same 16-reference URL set.
scope: Full Japanese source and all twelve translations. Compared complete available editions for meaning, terminology, applicable mathematics, code, and links. Non-English editions are intentionally concise and do not reproduce every derivation/subheading one-to-one.
